premise: I drained my $95,000 401(k) to buy a failing Greek diner with my daughter and son‑in‑law, taking a signed partnership agreement for a 40% stake and a salaried manager’s job; six months later they handed me a ‘revised’ contract that stripped my equity and fired me, claiming I’d only been a lender. I tipped off the IRS about their unreported cash catering side‑hustle, collected a $210,000 whistleblower reward, and bought the diner’s assets at the tax auction for $34,000 — now I run ‘Traitor’s Gyros’ in the same spot, and every receipt prints the IRS case number that proved they cooked the books.
